entries.base_behavior: Sections 5 and 28 list PressureRange + route-specific ExecutionBox BEFORE the nearest fresh structural target, while section 17.1 'Correct solve order' lists the target at step 3 and the route-specific structural entry interval at step 4; section 16.1 makes that interval the ExecutionBox, so both orders cannot hold.
entries.amended_behavior: Section 17.1 controls wherever the section 5 / 28 summary ordering conflicts with it. Structural target selection precedes route-specific ExecutionBox materialization. RouteEvaluation is not moved: section 17.1 step 2 still precedes the target; what is forbidden is forming the route-specific legal entry geometry before the canonical target is known.
entries.reason: Section 17.4 makes target_room_interval a member of the feasible-entry intersection, so selecting the target after the entry geometry exists would be circular; resolving it by code precedence would hide an authority decision inside an implementation.

entries.base_behavior: Section 17.2 requires the nearest structural target that is also not yet passed at decision time, but never states what nearest is measured from.
entries.amended_behavior: Origin is decision_price: the latest authoritative non-future price observation valid at the canonical decision_time, from strategy-side closed-price authority. Live broker quotes, future candle data, eventual fill prices, route-derived entry prices and RR-chosen reference prices are forbidden as origin. BUY eligible iff target_price > decision_price with distance target_price - decision_price; SELL eligible iff target_price < decision_price with distance decision_price - target_price. Not-passed is a pre-filter, not a tie-breaker. Zone comparison boundaries must be declared by the amendment that introduces a zone representation.
entries.reason: Measuring from the entry interval is circular with section 17.4.

entries.base_behavior: Section 17.2 requires fresh and never defines it; Audit/Replay v3 section 18.3 stores a freshness status and a tested count without transitions; section 11.6 forbids wall-clock age from being authority.
entries.amended_behavior: Freshness is a structural/source-policy state, not a clock. A wall-clock TTL is not canonical freshness authority and valid_until is reclassified NON_CANONICAL / ADVISORY_ONLY. The canonical selector predicate is freshness_status == FRESH. tested_count is evidence and implies no universal threshold. Each source class may form freshness differently provided the policy is explicit, deterministic, versioned, non-future and authority-approved, and the record carries a freshness_policy_id with its version. Freshness is not consumption. Literal field names are not mandated where equivalent provenance already exists, but the semantics of freshness_status, tested_count and the policy identity/version must not be lost.
entries.reason: A TTL cannot express tested-and-still-fresh, and a universal tested-count threshold would reintroduce the magic number A1-11 removed.

entries.base_behavior: Section 17.2 requires unconsumed, section 18.3 stores consumed_at and invalidated_at and section 21.6 has TARGET_CONSUMED, but nothing states what consumes a target.
entries.amended_behavior: Consumption is market-evidence truth: the authoritative price path satisfied the target's canonical completion condition. It is never ExecutionBox creation, TradePlanCandidate creation, risk approval, order submission, a broker fill or a position, and ExecutionBox.CONSUMED must not be imported. TEST is price interaction without completion and changes tested_count and possibly freshness, never consumption. For point targets consumed_at is the first authoritative target-completion evidence, with the completion rule source-policy-bound under the A2-03 discipline; this amendment fixes NO candle field as the criterion, so whether completion is a wick touch, a close through, a bid touch or an ask touch is NOT_DEFINED_BY_AUTHORITY and must not be chosen in an adapter. Zone target runtime semantics are NOT_ACTIVE because the canonical contract has no zone representation. The section 13 liquidity FSM is authority for the LIQUIDITY source only.
entries.reason: Without this separation a touch would silently consume a target and trade-lifecycle events would leak into market-evidence truth.

entries.base_behavior: Section 17.2 states the predicate in prose; read literally it is six conditions, not the four commonly quoted, because the quoted set omits authoritative, in-thesis-direction and not-passed-at-decision-time.
entries.amended_behavior: Canonical eligibility surface: STRUCTURAL and AUTHORITATIVE and IN THESIS DIRECTION and FRESH and UNCONSUMED and NOT PASSED AT decision_time. nearest is applied after all six filters and is never one of them. A farther target stays forbidden while a nearer one is active. Target selection never reads RR; an RR failure rejects the setup rather than selecting the next target.
entries.reason: The four-word shorthand loses three conditions that section 17.2 states explicitly.

entries.base_behavior: Authority requires the nearest target but says nothing about two eligible targets at equal distance.
entries.amended_behavior: Frozen from the existing selector rather than invented: primary key is the minimum positive directional distance from decision_price, secondary key is ascending target_id. formed_at is EXCLUDED because it would silently create an older-preferred or newer-preferred market semantics that no authority states. TargetSource precedence, RR precedence, timeframe precedence and any source-quality score are likewise excluded unless a later amendment authorises them. target_id carries no structural claim and must be stable, deterministic and independent of deployment, request or worker randomness; a non-deterministic target_id is a separate identity gap and must not be patched with formed_at.
entries.reason: Determinism must come from authority, not from an implementation detail.
